analysis:
The PR is documentation-only: docs/developer/build.md bumps the last-updated date and adds a paragraph at head lines 492-501 (the base text shows the insertion point near lines 489-492). The paragraph describes run-scoped Darkbloom CI runner labels. The route client sends X-Darkbloom-Run-Scoped-Labels: 1 and accepts a grant only when the profile label ends in -run-<github.run_id>, after any size suffix. A missing, generic or different-run label keeps the Blacksmith fallback. This tightens CI runner selection so a runner from an older workflow run cannot take a job. It stays fail-closed and does not broaden accepted labels.

I found no provider code, wire protocol, attestation, key custody or cache behavior changes, so none of the provider threats (T-041, TB-002/003/007/009/011 and others) are affected. The CI caching section (SAVE_CACHES, CI_ACTIONS_CACHE gating) is unchanged context in this diff.

Open integration question: the actual workflow code (.github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml, provider-plan.yml) and the sandbox plane are not in the supplied batch. I cannot verify that they implement the documented label check or the individual-job-retry behavior. This is a documentation claim, not a finding. The documented behavior is a stricter control than before, and the CI routing is outside the provider threat model's main assets.
